summary: Modular monolith Go on Azure Container Apps with Azure Database for PostgreSQL – Flexible Server as the database; front end: React + Vite.

architecture_rationale.text: One Go deployable split into internal modules: clear boundaries for 5 engineers without the operational cost of microservices; real-time sync runs as a separate process. Microservices rejected: 5 engineer(s) cannot absorb their operational overhead.

frontend.justification: A client-rendered app behind login needs no server rendering. Fit for this project: team.languages includes TypeScript; well suited to realtime collab projects; TypeScript is listed first (treated as the team's primary language); strong performance, which you rated 5/5.

tradeoffs: Client-rendered: no SEO for public pages.

supporting.justification: Multi-tenant B2B SaaS with social login: Auth0 Organizations models each customer team (invites, roles, per-tenant login) as a managed service, so engineering time goes into the product rather than running an IdP; the EU tenant keeps identity data in the EU for GDPR.

alternatives.why_not: No per-MAU fees, but the team must run, patch and back up an IdP.
Stores data in the US; weaker fit for GDPR-minded EU customers.

tradeoffs: Account recovery and MFA flows must still be designed.

supporting.justification: Per-seat plans, proration and invoices out of the box; Stripe Tax handles EU VAT.

alternatives.why_not: Merchant of record removes VAT work, but higher fees and less control.
Billing layer on top of a gateway: one more vendor.

tradeoffs: Gateway fees (~2% per transaction) are not part of the infra estimate.

supporting.justification: Clients upload directly with short-lived SAS tokens, so large files never pass through the API; objects are encrypted at rest and private by default.

alternatives.why_not: Cross-cloud egress and identity.

tradeoffs: Needs lifecycle rules to control growth.

supporting.justification: Caches uploaded media and static assets close to users and absorbs traffic spikes.

alternatives.why_not: Slower first loads for public pages and media.

supporting.choice: Yjs (CRDT) + Hocuspocus sync server (TypeScript), Redis pub/sub between nodes
supporting.justification: Concurrent edits to the same document/board must merge without conflicts: Yjs CRDTs do that, the Hocuspocus sync server syncs updates and awareness (live cursors, presence) over WebSockets, and Redis fans updates out across instances for 5000 concurrent users. Snapshots persist to Azure Database for PostgreSQL – Flexible Server.

alternatives.why_not: Managed and fast to start, but per-MAU pricing and US data storage.
Loses concurrent edits.

tradeoffs: Long-lived connections must be drained on deploys; size Redis pub/sub for peak fan-out.

supporting.justification: Caches hot reads and sessions to hold p95=100ms, and carries pub/sub for real-time fan-out.

alternatives.why_not: No pub/sub or persistence, so it cannot double as a broker.
Every read hits the database at peak.

tradeoffs: Another stateful component to size and monitor.

supporting.justification: Moves slow or retry-prone work (payment webhooks, image/file processing) off the request path so p95 stays low and failures retry safely.

alternatives.why_not: Event-streaming platform: heavy to run for job queues at this scale.

tradeoffs: Jobs must be idempotent; monitor the dead-letter queue.

supporting.justification: Runs tests and deploys on every merge; free minutes cover a small team.

alternatives.why_not: Self-hosted server to maintain.

supporting.choice: Azure Monitor + Application Insights + OpenTelemetry tracing
supporting.justification: Logs, metrics and traces stay in the same cloud and region as the data.

alternatives.why_not: Strong product but expensive per host at this budget.

assumptions: Scale level L3: ~50000 users, ~5000 peak concurrent, ~1000 req/s at peak, ~200 GB stored
Upper bound capped at ~3x the lower bound: components do not all reach their peak tier in the same month
List prices for the smallest production tier that fits; no reserved-instance or startup credits; excludes domains, app-store fees and payment-gateway transaction fees

warnings.message: The low estimate ($499) fits the $1500 budget, but the upper estimate ($1547) exceeds it as usage grows; set billing alerts and use the cost-control notes in each component.
Taking payments: use the gateway's hosted checkout/SDK so card data never touches your servers (PCI DSS SAQ A).
GDPR: an EU region is the simplest option; otherwise rely on the provider's DPA and SCCs.
